daily.title: Cash Deposit Addition Alone Cannot Sustain Property Investment Reassessment: ITAT Delhi
daily.summary: ITAT Delhi quashes Rs. 46.95 lakh Section 69A addition as reassessment concerned property investment but AO taxed only unexplained bank deposits. In Tsering Dolkar Vs ITO, Ward 1(1)(3), Dehradun , decided on 20 November 2026 for AY 2016–17, the Delhi ITAT quashed a reassessment that had been initiated for an alleged undisclosed investment in immovable property but culminated in an addition only for unexplained bank deposits under Section 69A . Although the same bank information figured in the reopening proceedings, the order under Section 148A(d) expressly identified a property investment as the escaped income.

daily.title: Faceless Proceedings Difficulties Justify Condonation of 1,384-Day Delay: ITAT Delhi
daily.summary: ITAT Delhi condones 1,384-day appeal delay due to faceless procedure difficulties and inadequate representation, remanding Section 271(1)(c) penalty matter. In Sandeep Kumar Vs ITO, Ward 47(1), Delhi , decided on 20 November 2026 for AY 2012–13, the Delhi ITAT condoned a delay of about 1,384 days in filing an appeal before the CIT(A)/NFAC. The Tribunal accepted that the assessee’s unfamiliarity with faceless procedures, inadequate representation and financial and business difficulties together constituted sufficient cause.

daily.title: Reassessment Void Without Mandatory Section 143(2) Notice: ITAT Delhi
daily.summary: ITAT Delhi quashes reassessment despite fresh assessment on remand as AO failed to issue mandatory Section 143(2) notice after considering the return. In Lalit Chaudhary Vs ITO, Ward 43(6), New Delhi , decided on 20 November 2026 for AY 2016–17, the Delhi ITAT held that a notice under Section 143(2) was mandatory where the Assessing Officer took cognisance of the return filed in response to Section 148 and proceeded to assess income above the returned figure. The electronic proceedings record established that the officer issued a questionnaire under Section 142(1) but omitted the jurisdictional notice.
